angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 228,885 km at 19.86 pc = 0.15 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 50.3399 +/- 0.0151 mas (same row, RUWE 1.12): 19.86 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.329 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Silverstein et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of LHS 1678 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..151S/abstract): 228,885 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.345 +/- 0.014 solar masses from Silverstein et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of LHS 1678 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..151S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3490 +/- 50 K from Silverstein et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 1678 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..151S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Silverstein et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 1678 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..151S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/lhs-1678.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.941, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1678 (pscomppars): spectral type M2.0 V, from Silverstein et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..151S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1678 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.83863, from Silverstein et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..151S/abstract)
